p.i: illi nouerunt tuam intemperantiam, & te non obseruare si quid mandent. Si mihi certò promittis, te obedientem fore meis mandatis, ego te sanabo. Rusticus promittit. Medicus respondet: Abstineas decem dies saltem à potu, & melius habebis. Non enim siti morieris. Rusticus discedit, & obedit: & elapso octiduo, reuertitur sanus in myropolium, indicatq́; Medico quis sit: ac interrogat quid ulterius ipsi sit faciendum, an adhuc diutius à potu abstinere debeat: quia iam se esse assuefactum, ut facile sitim ferre possit. Medicus iubet, ut non multum bibat, sed singulis diebus cantharum. Tantum consuetudo valet.

Ioachimus Kirsser, medicinæ Doctor & Physicus principis Ernesti Marchionis Badensis, simili ratione ignoranter rusticum hydropicum curauit. Rusticus conueniens medicum, petiit sibi dari consilium, quod in hydropisi sequi posset. Cui Medicus iocosè his uerbis respondit: Si in semestri spacio à potu abstineres, facile curareris. Rusticus existimans hæc à Doctore seriò dicta

page.notes: The left-edge fragments of the facing page are cut off and mostly illegible; the running head "MEDICVS" is set in spaced capitals with a period. The catchword "dicta" is taken as the last word of the final line, which is a full line, so it is also given as catchword. Some letters in the italic text (e.g. "iocosè", "petiit") are read with reasonable confidence; no doubtful words were marked.
